stories.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
stories.summary: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.
stories.detail: Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights. In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning , the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.

details.summary: The law faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.

stories.title: Spain to vote in election that could put far right in power for first time since Franco
stories.summary: Socialist PM Pedro Sánchez’s high-stakes gamble could end in defeat to a coalition including the far-right Vox Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday to vote in a high-stakes snap general election that could put a far-right party in government for the first…
stories.detail: Socialist PM Pedro Sánchez’s high-stakes gamble could end in defeat to a coalition including the far-right Vox Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday to vote in a high-stakes snap general election that could put a far-right party in government for the first time since the country’s return to democracy after the death of Gen Francisco Franco in 1975. Although the next election was not due until summer next year, Spain’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, called the vote in October after three rightwing and far-right parties voted down the emergency legislation that his government had proposed to address the country’s housing crisis .
